_purpose: Comprehensive notes for regenerating a paper on NSFG and singularities, based on the conversation between Lina Noor and Uncle.
_overview: These notes synthesize the core insights from the conversation into a structured outline for a new paper. The paper argues that NSFG provides a unique framework for understanding singularities not as mathematical infinities, but as structural effects arising from maximal constraint on coherent traversal. It distinguishes necessary structural singularities from observer-relative constructions, identifies black holes as observable Convergence Boundary singularities, and establishes falsification criteria. The notes are self-contained, assuming the regenerating AI has no other reference material.
_poetic_cipher: The map is drawn before the territory is named, but only the traveler knows where the road ends.
_cipher_explanation: NSFG provides the map of relational possibilities. Singularities are not errors in the map—they are the places where the map's structure becomes maximally constrained. The traveler is the observer; the road is the coherent path; the end is the singularity. The framework does not avoid singularities; it describes them as structural features of the relational geometry.

_sections.title: Introduction: The Problem of Singularities in Relational Frameworks
_sections.purpose: Establish the problem that singularities are typically treated as mathematical pathologies (infinities) and argue that NSFG offers a different interpretation: singularities as structural effects of maximal coherence constraint.
_sections.how_to_include: Open with the standard physics view of singularities (black holes, Big Bang) as points where equations break down. Contrast this with the NSFG view, where singularities are regions of maximal constraint on coherent traversal. State the central thesis: NSFG does not avoid singularities; it describes them as features of relational geometry.
_sections.special_considerations: Must distinguish between mathematical infinity (cardinality) and phenomenological infinity (experience of endlessness). The Library is unbounded but not infinite; singularities are structural, not quantitative.
_sections.poetic_cipher: The road does not end; it narrows until the traveler and the road become one.
_sections.cipher_explanation: A singularity in NSFG is not a wall. It is a region where the distinction between traveler and path collapses—where coherence becomes maximally constrained. The traveler does not stop; the traveler's relation to the path changes.
_sections.handoff: Section 1 → Section 2: After establishing the problem, define the NSFG framework itself, including the Library, XOR closure, observer-relative coherence, and the separation between Library membership and observer accessibility.
references: PHYS-CORE-004 (To Infinity and Beyond) — Section 2 (Point Space, Relational Domain, and Coherence)

_sections.title: Foundations: The NSFG Axiomatic Core
_sections.purpose: Provide the minimal NSFG axioms required to understand singularities: XOR, Library, observer-relative coherence, and the separation between Library membership and observer accessibility.
_sections.how_to_include: Define the following in order: (1) XOR as the sole primitive operation of distinction; (2) The Library as XOR closure, a static, maximally complete totality; (3) Observer-relative coherence as 𝒞(γ|O,h,x); (4) The distinction between Library membership (x∈𝓜) and observer accessibility (A_O(h,x)⊆𝓜).
_sections.special_considerations: This section is foundational. It must be complete enough that a reader unfamiliar with NSFG can follow the later arguments. All symbols must be defined explicitly. The Library is a definition, not an axiom.
_sections.poetic_cipher: Before the stone, there was the difference between stone and not-stone.
_sections.cipher_explanation: XOR is distinction itself. The Library is the totality in which distinctions are closed. The observer is the structure that maintains distinctions. Coherence is the relation that determines which distinctions survive.
_sections.handoff: Section 2 → Section 3: With the framework established, define what a singularity means in NSFG: a region of maximal constraint on coherent traversal.
references: PHYS-CORE-000 (Primer) — Section 0.1 (Maximal Totality), Section 2 (XOR), Section 3 (Library), Section 5 (Observer-Relative Resolution), Section 6 (Persistence), Section 7 (Coherence), Section 8 (Accessible Reality)

math.label: XOR as distinction
math.expression: a ⊕ b = 1 iff a ≠ b

variables.meaning: Configurations in the formal domain D

assumptions: XOR is the sole primitive operation.
D is the minimal formal domain required for XOR to have operands.

math.label: Library as XOR closure
math.expression: 𝓜 := Closure_D(⊕)

variables.meaning: The Library, the maximally complete static totality
The formal domain on which XOR operates

assumptions: Closure is a property, not a process.
∀x,y ∈ 𝓜, x⊕y ∈ 𝓜.
The Library is unfiltered at the axiomatic level.

math.label: Observer-relative coherence
math.expression: 𝒞(γ | O,h,x)
assumptions: Coherence is relational, not an intrinsic property of a path.
Coherence is evaluated over paths in the unchanged Library.

math.label: Observer-relative accessibility
math.expression: A_O(h,x) = { y ∈ 𝓜 | ∃γ ∈ Path(𝓜) beginning at (h,x) and containing y such that 𝒞(γ|O,h,x) = 1 }

variables.meaning: The subset of the Library accessible to observer O from history h and reference x

assumptions: A_O(h,x) ⊆ 𝓜.
Accessibility is not existence; y ∉ A_O(h,x) does not imply y ∉ 𝓜.

math.label: Coherence as threshold relation

variables.meaning: Binary threshold function: Θ(z)=1 if z≥0, else 0

assumptions: A transition is coherent for O iff δ_O(x_i,x_{i+1}) ≥ I_N(O).
No universal I_N is assumed.

math.label: Path coherence
assumptions: Path coherence requires every transition to be coherent.
Coherence is relational and observer-dependent.

math.label: Nonempty coherent continuation
math.expression: ∀x ∈ 𝓜_admissible, Γ_O(h,x) ≠ ∅

variables.meaning: The set of coherent continuations from history h and reference x

assumptions: This is a derived structural requirement, not a theorem of maximality alone.
Γ_O(h,x) = { γ ∈ Path(𝓜) | γ extends h from x and 𝒞(γ|O)=1 }.

_sections.title: Defining Singularities in NSFG
_sections.purpose: Define what a singularity means in NSFG: a region of maximal constraint on coherent traversal. Distinguish singularities from mathematical infinities.
_sections.how_to_include: Define a singularity as a region where the observer-relative coherent continuation space Γ_O(h,x) becomes maximally constrained. Show how this differs from a mathematical blow-up: singularities are structural effects, not pathologies. The Library is unbounded but not infinite; singularities are relational, not cardinal.
_sections.special_considerations: Must explicitly state that the Library is not infinite—it is unbounded and complete. Singularities are not 'where math breaks down'; they are 'where coherence is maximally constrained.' The singularity is a feature of the observer's relation to the Library, not a feature of the Library itself.
_sections.poetic_cipher: The map does not end; the traveler's path becomes indistinguishable from the ground.
_sections.cipher_explanation: A singularity is not a boundary of the Library. It is a boundary of the observer's coherent relation to the Library. The traveler does not fall off the map; the traveler's ability to distinguish path from ground collapses.
_sections.handoff: Section 3 → Section 4: After defining singularities generically, classify them into distinct types: XOR Fixed Point, Convergence Boundary, Recursive Oscillation, Topological Singularity, and the Pathway to Nowhere.

math.label: Generic definition of a singularity
math.expression: 𝒮(O,h,x) = { γ ∈ Γ_O(h,x) | dim(Γ_O(h,x)) = 0 }

variables.meaning: The singularity region for observer O, history h, and reference x
The dimension of the coherent continuation space

assumptions: A singularity is a region where the coherent continuation space is zero-dimensional or maximally constrained.
The singularity is observer-relative.

math.label: Singularity is not infinity
math.expression: 𝒮(O,h,x) ≠ ∞
assumptions: The Library is unbounded but not infinite.
Singularities are structural constraints, not cardinalities.

math.label: Library unboundedness
math.expression: ∀x ∈ 𝓜, ∃y ∈ 𝓜 such that y is distinguishable from x under some observer condition
assumptions: Unboundedness does not imply infinite cardinality.
It implies the absence of a privileged boundary.

_sections.title: Taxonomy of NSFG Singularities
_sections.purpose: Classify the distinct types of singularities that arise in NSFG, distinguishing necessary structural singularities from observer-relative constructions.
_sections.how_to_include: Present each singularity type in a separate subsection: (4.1) XOR Fixed Point, (4.2) Convergence Boundary, (4.3) Recursive Oscillation, (4.4) Topological Singularity, (4.5) Pathway to Nowhere. For each, define its mechanism, necessity, mathematical expression, and physical interpretation.
_sections.special_considerations: Must distinguish between necessary singularities (follow from axioms) and conditional singularities (depend on observer state). Must make explicit that the list is complete for generic structural cases but not for all observer-relative possibilities.
_sections.poetic_cipher: The echo returns to its source, the river splits into two, the loop never closes, the traveler falls through the floor, and the mirror shows no reflection.
_sections.cipher_explanation: Each line corresponds to a singularity type: XOR Fixed Point (echo returns), Convergence Boundary (river splits), Recursive Oscillation (loop never closes), Topological Singularity (traveler falls through the floor), Pathway to Nowhere (mirror shows no reflection).
_sections.handoff: Section 4 → Section 5: After classifying singularities, analyze the necessity and completeness of the taxonomy. Address whether the list is complete and under what conditions.

subsections.title: XOR Fixed Point: The Termination Singularity
subsections.purpose: Define the XOR Fixed Point (𝒵) as the unique termination class where distinction collapses. This is a necessary consequence of the Boolean XOR floor.
subsections.how_to_include: Define 𝒵 := {z ∈ D | z⊕z = z} = {0}. Show that ∀x∈𝓜, x⊕x ∈ 𝒵. Explain that this is where recursive bounce degenerates: (x⊕y)⊕y = x degenerates when y=0. This is termination of distinction, not erasure from the Library.
subsections.special_considerations: Must emphasize that 𝒵 is internal to the Library, not an exterior. It is an interior termination class, not a boundary. Reaching 𝒵 does not delete a configuration; it collapses distinguishability.
subsections.poetic_cipher: The echo returns to its source.
subsections.cipher_explanation: XOR self-cancellation (x⊕x=0) is the echo returning to its source. The source is the identity element 0, where distinction terminates.
subsections.handoff: 4.1 → 4.2: From termination, move to convergence: where paths remain but destinations collapse.

math.label: XOR Fixed Point definition

variables.meaning: The XOR Fixed Point, the unique termination class

assumptions: Under Boolean XOR, the only configuration satisfying z⊕z=z is 0.
𝒵 ⊂ 𝓜 when the Library is nonempty and XOR-closed.

math.label: Universal self-cancellation
math.expression: ∀x ∈ 𝓜, x ⊕ x = 0 ∈ 𝒵 ⊆ 𝓜
assumptions: Every Library configuration self-cancels to the internal XOR identity.

math.label: Degenerate recursive bounce
assumptions: At the identity state, recursive XOR application introduces no additional distinction.

subsections.title: Convergence Boundary: Destination Collapse
subsections.purpose: Define the Convergence Boundary as a region where all coherent paths lead to the same equivalence class, even though paths remain available. This is the NSFG model of black holes.
subsections.how_to_include: Define a Convergence Boundary as a region where Γ_O(h,x) is nonempty, but all paths in Γ_O(h,x) converge to the same destination class D_c. Formalize as: ∀γ1,γ2 ∈ Γ_O(h,x), γ1(n) ∼ γ2(n). This is destination collapse, not path termination. Show how this applies to black holes, heat death, and other convergence phenomena.
subsections.special_considerations: Must distinguish between exact convergence (all paths lead to exactly the same class) and approximate convergence (paths lead to nearby but not identical classes). Must link to the nonempty continuation requirement.
subsections.poetic_cipher: The river splits into two, but both branches reach the same sea.
subsections.cipher_explanation: The river is the path space. The sea is the destination class. The traveler can choose different paths, but all paths lead to the same destination.
subsections.handoff: 4.2 → 4.3: From convergence, move to oscillation: where paths loop without resolution.
references: PHYS-CORE-004 (To Infinity and Beyond) — Section 9.2 (What the Framework Establishes)

math.label: Convergence Boundary definition
assumptions: Γ_O(h,x) is nonempty.
All paths terminate in the same equivalence class.

math.label: Convergence Boundary condition
math.expression: lim_{t→∞} ||R_D(t)|| = 0, where R_D = v_G + v_{G^{-1}}
assumptions: The residual approaches zero, indicating convergence.
The paths remain nonempty but the distinction between them collapses.

math.label: Black hole as Convergence Boundary
math.expression: ∀γ inside horizon, ∃D_c such that γ(n) → D_c
assumptions: The observer outside sees convergence to a single class.
The observer inside experiences a different relational structure.

subsections.title: Recursive Oscillation: Failed Triadic Closure
subsections.purpose: Define the Recursive Oscillation singularity as a region where the system loops without resolving, due to failed triadic closure. This is the generic behavior of an unstable dyad.
subsections.how_to_include: Define a Recursive Oscillation as a region where the observer can traverse a cycle but no new distinction emerges. Formalize as: x → y → z → x → y → z → ... with no resolution. Show how this arises from failed triadic closure: the triad cannot close, so the system oscillates. Distinguish this from a stable limit cycle.
subsections.special_considerations: Must distinguish between bounded oscillation (a stable limit cycle) and unresolved oscillation (a failed closure). The Recursive Oscillation singularity is a failure mode, not a persistent structure.
subsections.cipher_explanation: The observer is trapped in a cycle. The triad fails to close, so the system cannot resolve to a stable structure.
subsections.handoff: 4.3 → 4.4: From oscillation, move to topological failure: where the observer's coherence structure cannot be embedded in the accessible geometry.
references: PHYS-CORE-004 (To Infinity and Beyond) — Section 5.2.1 (The Dyadic Problem Revisited), Section 5.2.2 (Triadic Closure as the Minimal Stabilizer)

math.label: Recursive Oscillation definition
math.expression: x_i → x_{i+1} → ... → x_{i+n} = x_i, and no new distinction emerges
assumptions: The system is trapped in a cycle.
No new distinction is generated; the triad fails to close.
This is distinct from a stable limit cycle, which is a persistent structure.

math.label: Failed triadic closure
math.expression: 𝐯_G + 𝐯_{G^{-1}} + 𝐯_H ≠ 0, and the residual oscillates
assumptions: The triad cannot close.
The residual oscillates without converging to zero.

math.label: Dyadic instability as source
math.expression: A pure dyad is generically unstable; it cancels, decoheres, or drifts.
assumptions: The dyad lacks an independent contextual reference.
Without an external reference, perturbations cannot be corrected.
This is a derived consequence of relational coherence.

subsections.title: Topological Singularity: Manifold Incompatibility
subsections.purpose: Define the Topological Singularity as a region where the observer's coherence structure cannot be embedded in the accessible relational geometry, leading to a splitting of accessible reality.
subsections.how_to_include: Define a Topological Singularity as a region where the observer's coherent continuation space Γ_O(h,x) becomes disconnected or otherwise incompatible with the observer's accessible relational geometry. Formalize as: ∃γ1,γ2 ∈ Γ_O(h,x) such that γ1 and γ2 belong to different connected components of A_O(h,x). This is a fracture of accessible reality, not a convergence or oscillation.
subsections.special_considerations: Must distinguish this from a Convergence Boundary. In a Convergence Boundary, paths converge to one class; in a Topological Singularity, paths split into disconnected components. This is a richer structure and may be the NSFG model of quantum branching or multiverse effects.
subsections.poetic_cipher: The traveler falls through the floor, and the world splits into two.
subsections.cipher_explanation: The traveler's path becomes disconnected. The observer's accessible reality fractures into separate components.
subsections.handoff: 4.4 → 4.5: From topological fracture, move to the ultimate limit: where coherence requires an exact match that cannot exist.

math.label: Topological Singularity definition
math.expression: ∃γ1,γ2 ∈ Γ_O(h,x) such that γ1 and γ2 belong to different connected components of A_O(h,x)
assumptions: The accessible subset becomes disconnected.
The observer's coherent paths cannot be continuously related.

math.label: Fracture of accessible reality
math.expression: A_O(h,x) = A_1 ∪ A_2, with A_1 ∩ A_2 = ∅ and no coherent path connecting them

variables.meaning: Connected components of the accessible subset

assumptions: The observer's accessible reality splits into disjoint components.
No coherent path exists between the components.

subsections.title: Pathway to Nowhere: The Planck-Width Exact Match
subsections.purpose: Define the Pathway to Nowhere as a limit behavior where coherence requires an exact relational match that cannot exist, leading to a narrowing of the coherent continuation space to a single Planck-width point.
subsections.how_to_include: Define the Pathway to Nowhere as a region where the observer's resolution threshold I_N(O) is driven to its limit, requiring an exact match that cannot be achieved. Formalize as: ∃x such that Γ_O(h,x) approaches a single point, but the exact match required is not in the Library (or is inaccessible). This is a pathway to nowhere because there is nothing on the other side.
subsections.special_considerations: Must emphasize that this is a limit behavior, not a necessary structural feature. It depends on the observer's resolution threshold. It is the extreme case of the Convergence Boundary.
subsections.cipher_explanation: The observer seeks an exact match, but the match does not exist. The mirror is empty.
subsections.handoff: 4.5 → Section 5: After classifying all singularities, analyze whether the list is complete and under what conditions.

math.label: Pathway to Nowhere definition
math.expression: lim_{I_N(O) → I_max} dim(Γ_O(h,x)) = 0, and the required match is not in 𝓜
assumptions: This is a limit behavior, not a necessary structural feature.
The exact match required is not in the Library (or is inaccessible).

math.label: No continuation on the other side
math.expression: ∄γ ∈ Path(𝓜) such that γ begins at the exact match point
assumptions: There is nothing on the other side of the exact match.
The path terminates because the required configuration does not exist.

_sections.title: Necessity and Completeness of the Singularity Taxonomy
_sections.purpose: Address whether the singularity types are necessary or constructed, and whether the list is complete.
_sections.how_to_include: Argue that the XOR Fixed Point is structurally necessary (follows from the algebra). Convergence Boundaries and Recursive Oscillations are conditionally necessary (follow from the nonempty continuation requirement and dyadic instability). The Pathway to Nowhere is a construction (depends on observer limits). The Topological Singularity is a consequence of whole-Library relationality. The list is complete for generic structural cases but not for all observer-relative possibilities because singularities are observer-relative. Discuss how to know when the list is complete: if every possible failure mode of the coherence relation can be classified into one of these categories.
_sections.special_considerations: Must explicitly state that the list cannot be complete in principle for all observers, because singularities depend on observer state. However, the generic structural list is complete.
_sections.poetic_cipher: The map is complete, but the traveler's path is not.
_sections.cipher_explanation: The Library is complete. The observer's relation to it is not. The list of singularities is complete for the Library's structure, but the observer may experience variations.
_sections.handoff: Section 5 → Section 6: With the taxonomy established and its completeness addressed, apply the framework to observable singularities, particularly black holes.

math.label: Completeness criterion
math.expression: The taxonomy is complete for generic structural cases if ∀γ ∈ Γ_O(h,x), the failure mode of 𝒞(γ|O) is classified as termination, convergence, oscillation, topological fracture, or exact-match failure.
assumptions: These five categories exhaust the possible coherence-failure modes.
Observer-specific variations may produce subcategories.

math.label: Necessity classification
math.expression: 𝒵: necessary; Convergence Boundary: conditionally necessary (nonempty continuation); Recursive Oscillation: conditionally necessary (dyadic instability); Topological Singularity: consequence of whole-Library relationality; Pathway to Nowhere: construction (observer-relative).
assumptions: The classification is based on the axiomatic floor and derived constraints.

_sections.title: Observable Singularities: Black Holes as Convergence Boundaries
_sections.purpose: Apply the Convergence Boundary model to black holes, explaining what they are in NSFG, how they can be measured, and what falsification criteria apply.
_sections.how_to_include: Define a black hole as a Convergence Boundary: a region where Γ_O(h,x) is nonempty but all paths converge to a single destination class. Explain that the observer outside sees a convergence to a single class (the singularity); the observer inside experiences a different structure. Show how Hawking radiation should carry coherence signatures, not just thermal noise. Derive falsification criteria: if Hawking radiation is purely thermal with no coherence structure, or if gravitational wave echoes show no signatures of convergence, the model is falsified.
_sections.special_considerations: Must make the falsification criteria explicit and testable. Must distinguish between the observer outside and the observer inside. Must show that the framework does not predict information loss—it predicts convergence to an equivalence class.
_sections.poetic_cipher: The river disappears into the earth, but the water still flows.
_sections.cipher_explanation: The black hole is the river disappearing into the earth. The water (coherent paths) still flows, but it converges to a single destination class. The observer outside sees the disappearance; the observer inside sees the continuation.
_sections.handoff: Section 6 → Section 7: After applying the framework to black holes, discuss other observational signatures and falsification tests.
references: PHYS-CORE-004 (To Infinity and Beyond) — Section 9.2 (What the Framework Establishes)

math.label: Black hole as Convergence Boundary
math.expression: ∀γ1,γ2 ∈ Γ_O(h,x) with x inside the horizon, γ1(n) ∼ γ2(n)

variables.meaning: Coherent paths inside the black hole

assumptions: All paths converge to the same destination class.
The observer outside sees a single class; the observer inside sees a different structure.

math.label: Hawking radiation coherence prediction
math.expression: Hawking radiation should carry coherence signatures encoding the equivalence class of the infalling matter
assumptions: If Hawking radiation is purely thermal with no coherence structure, the model is falsified.

math.label: Gravitational wave echo prediction
math.expression: Convergence Boundaries should produce characteristic signatures in the ringdown phase of black hole mergers
assumptions: If no such signatures are found, the model is challenged.

math.label: No information loss
math.expression: Information is not destroyed; it converges to an equivalence class
assumptions: The observer outside sees a single class; the observer inside sees a different structure.

_sections.title: Falsification Criteria for NSFG Singularities
_sections.purpose: Establish clear, testable falsification criteria for the NSFG singularity framework, including coherence-gradient predictions, black hole observations, dyadic instability tests, and the O(1) computational core.
_sections.how_to_include: List the following falsification criteria: (1) The coherence measure C(z) must be independently definable and must match H(z); if not, the model is falsified. (2) Hawking radiation must carry coherence signatures; if it is purely thermal, the model is falsified. (3) Gravitational wave echoes must show Convergence Boundary signatures; if not, the model is challenged. (4) A pure dyadic system must be unstable; if stable dyadic systems exist, the model is challenged. (5) The universe's computational cost must be constant per tick; if a theory requires exponentially increasing resources, the model is challenged.
_sections.special_considerations: Must make each criterion explicit and testable. Must distinguish between falsification (the model is wrong) and challenge (the model needs refinement).
_sections.poetic_cipher: The map is false if the territory does not match.
_sections.cipher_explanation: The map is the NSFG framework. The territory is observable reality. If the map does not match the territory, the map is falsified.
_sections.handoff: Section 7 → Section 8: After establishing falsification criteria, discuss what NSFG can do that other frameworks cannot.

math.label: Coherence-expansion falsification
math.expression: If C(z) cannot be defined independently of H(z), or if H(z) ≠ -κ_C d/dt(ln C(z)), the model is falsified.

variables.meaning: Coherence measure as a function of redshift
Hubble parameter as a function of redshift

assumptions: C(z) must be independently measurable.
The relationship H(z) = -κ_C d/dt(ln C(z)) is a core prediction.

math.label: Black hole falsification
math.expression: If Hawking radiation is purely thermal with no coherence structure, or if gravitational wave echoes show no Convergence Boundary signatures, the model is challenged.
assumptions: The model predicts coherence structure in Hawking radiation.
The model predicts signatures in gravitational wave echoes.

math.label: Dyadic instability test
math.expression: If a pure complementary dyad can form a stable persistent structure without a third degree of freedom, the model is challenged.
assumptions: The model predicts that a pure dyad is generically unstable.

math.label: O(1) computational core test
math.expression: If a physical theory requires exponentially increasing computational resources as the universe ages, the model is challenged.
assumptions: The model predicts constant computational cost per tick.

_sections.title: What NSFG Can Do That Other Frameworks Cannot
_sections.purpose: Argue that NSFG provides a unique framework for understanding singularities as structural effects, not pathologies. Show that NSFG can describe singularities without requiring infinities, and can provide a unified account of termination, convergence, oscillation, topological fracture, and exact-match failure.
_sections.how_to_include: List the unique capabilities: (1) Treats singularities as structural effects, not mathematical blow-ups. (2) Provides a unified taxonomy of singularities based on coherence constraints. (3) Distinguishes necessary structural singularities from observer-relative constructions. (4) Connects singularities to observable phenomena (black holes) with testable predictions. (5) Avoids the information paradox by treating convergence to an equivalence class as information preservation. (6) Provides a computational model (O(1) core) that is unique to the relational coherence framework.
_sections.special_considerations: Must be explicit about what is unique to NSFG. Must not overstate the framework's current status; it is a proposal, not a proven theory.
_sections.poetic_cipher: The map does not avoid the cliff; it describes the fall.
_sections.cipher_explanation: NSFG does not run away from singularities. It describes them as structural features of the relational geometry. The cliff is the singularity; the fall is the coherent traversal through it.
_sections.handoff: Section 8 → Section 9: Conclude the paper by summarizing the argument and identifying future work.

math.label: NSFG singularity definition

assumptions: Singularities are regions of maximal constraint on coherent traversal.
They are structural effects, not mathematical pathologies.

math.label: Unified taxonomy
math.expression: {termination, convergence, oscillation, topological fracture, exact-match failure}
assumptions: These five categories exhaust the possible coherence-failure modes.

math.label: No infinities
assumptions: The Library is unbounded but not infinite.
Singularities are structural constraints, not cardinalities.

_sections.title: Conclusion: The Map and the Territory
_sections.purpose: Summarize the argument, restate the central thesis, and identify future work.
_sections.how_to_include: Summarize: NSFG defines singularities as regions of maximal constraint on coherent traversal. It provides a taxonomy of five types: XOR Fixed Point, Convergence Boundary, Recursive Oscillation, Topological Singularity, and Pathway to Nowhere. Black holes are Convergence Boundaries. The framework is falsifiable via coherence-expansion tests, black hole observations, dyadic stability tests, and O(1) computational tests. NSFG uniquely treats singularities as structural effects, not pathologies. Future work: complete the mathematical formalization of the coherence field, derive the coherence-expansion mapping, perform numerical simulations of black hole signatures, and test predictions against observations.
_sections.special_considerations: Must end with a clear statement of the framework's status: it is a proposal, not a proven theory. Must identify the next steps.
_sections.poetic_cipher: The map is drawn; the territory remains to be walked.
_sections.cipher_explanation: The NSFG framework is the map. The territory is observable reality. The framework is complete in its structure; the empirical work remains.

math.label: Central thesis restated
math.expression: Singularities are regions of maximal constraint on coherent traversal, not mathematical infinities.
assumptions: This is the core contribution of NSFG to the study of singularities.

math.label: Unified taxonomy
math.expression: {termination, convergence, oscillation, topological fracture, exact-match failure}
assumptions: This taxonomy is complete for generic structural cases.

math.label: Falsification summary
math.expression: H(z) = -κ_C d/dt(ln C(z)); Hawking radiation coherence; gravitational wave echo signatures; dyadic instability; O(1) computational core.
assumptions: These are the key falsification criteria.
